newsitem.title: USA: Clinton declares disaster in Alabama.
newsitem.headline: Clinton declares disaster in Alabama.

text.p: President Clinton Friday declared parts of Alabama hit by Hurricane Danny major disaster areas, making individuals and local governments eligible for federal aid.

The declaration applies to Baldwin, Choctaw and Mobile counties. Assistance can include housing, grants, low-cost loans and other programmes to help in the aftermath of the hurricane, which brought severe storms, flooding and high winds to the area this week.

"Know that we will stand by you and help you in every way we can," Clinton said in a written statement. "Our hearts and prayers are with those who suffered losses and we wish you Godspeed in your recovery."
The president also declared parts of Vermont and Montana hit by severe storms and flooding major disaster areas, making them eligible for federal aid.
The declaration applies to Caledonia, Franklin, Lamoille, Orleans and Washington counties in Vermont, which were struck by excessive rainfall, high winds and flooding July 15-17.

In Montana, local governments in 17 counties hit by storms, ice jams, snowmelt, flooding and extreme soil saturation since March 1 will be eligible for federal assistance, the White House said in a written statement.
